blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless heater heats water only when a tap opens. Water flows through a heat exchanger, a burner or element heats it on demand and it goes straight to the fixture. There's no stored tank to keep hot, so there's no standby heat loss, and you don't run out partway through a shower. What limits a tankless unit is flow: it can heat only so many gallons per minute, so it's sized to how many fixtures you run at once.

blocks.h2: Is Tankless a Good Fit for Your Elgin Home?
blocks.intro: Here's what decides whether tankless fits your Elgin home. Here's what decides the fit.

items.body: Tankless units draw a lot of gas when they fire. Older homes often have a gas line sized for a furnace and a tank heater. We check before quoting.
Tankless units vent through a wall or the roof with their own pipe. In historic homes with stone or thick masonry walls, we plan the route carefully.
Minerals in treated water build up in the heat exchanger. We install service valves so regular descaling is quick.

items.q: How often should a tankless water heater be descaled?
items.preview: Regularly, based on your water and use. Often once a year.
items.answer: Most manufacturers call for regular descaling, often about once a year, more with heavy use. It keeps the unit efficient and protects the warranty.

items.q: My tankless heater shows an error code. Can you fix it?
items.preview: Yes. Most codes point to a specific part or a maintenance need.
items.answer: Yes. Error codes usually point to ignition, flame, flow or scale problems. Tell us the code when you call, and we'll come prepared.

items.q: Can a tankless unit run my whole house?
items.preview: Usually, if it's sized for your peak use.
items.answer: Usually, yes. A properly sized unit handles a couple of showers and an appliance at once. Large homes may need a bigger unit or two.

items.q: Will I need a new gas line?
items.preview: Sometimes. We check the size and length before we quote.
items.answer: Sometimes. Many older homes need a larger line to the heater. We check the existing line and include any upgrade in the flat price.

items.answer: It depends on the unit, whether the gas line needs upsizing and the venting. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
